name: M2.coulomb_viscous
title: Coulomb and viscous friction
summary: Constant (Coulomb) plus viscous friction at the output, fitted from measurements: MuJoCo's frictionloss and damping, so its simulator is optional.

output.name: tau_r
output.definition: The resisting torque at the output: what the motor must add to move the output as the inputs say.
output.sign: The joint feels -tau_r (a resisting torque opposes motion; ripple pushes and pulls with angle).

coulomb_friction.measured_by: velocity plateaus, both directions, 6-8 speeds, each at least one rotor turn

viscous_friction.measured_by: velocity plateaus, both directions, 6-8 speeds, each at least one rotor turn

python.note: The contract's own ruler: stdlib Python, torque(terms, inputs, state, dt) -> (tau_r, state), terms in SI.

js.note: The same equation as model.py as an ES module (torque(terms, inputs, state, dt) -> {tau, state}); tests/acceptance_v2/test_amendment_2_5.py holds the two to 1e-12.

friction_solref.definition: The joint's solreffriction (timeconst, dampratio): how hard frictionloss sticks; MuJoCo's soft default creeps below about 0.4 rad/s on a light hinge.

friction_solimp.definition: The joint's solimpfriction (dmin, dmax, width, midpoint, power), every entry > 0.

mujoco.note: frictionloss sticks at rest as a constraint (set friction_solref hard, or it creeps); damping is the viscous term.

output_speed.definition: |v|, the output speed the terms were fitted or checked across.

assumptions: Friction does not depend on speed beyond the viscous slope, on load, on temperature or on how long the part rested.
